merger_description:
SCM Financial Group Pty Ltd (**SCM**) proposes to acquire all the business and client related assets of the Strategic Wealth Services Group, which comprises the following 3 entities:

* Strategic Financial Planners Pty Ltd, a provider of financial planning services;
* Strategic Accountants and Business Advisors Pty Ltd as trustee for the Strategic Accountants & Business Advisors Unit Trust, a provider of tax, accounting and business services; and
* Strategic Super Services Pty Ltd as trustee for the S3 Strategic Super Services Unit Trust, a provider of self-managed superannuation fund accounting services.

SCM is a provider of financial planning, tax & accounting services and lending services with 2 offices in Surrey Hills in Victoria and St Leonards in New South Wales. SCM is a wholly owned subsidiary of AZ Next Generation Advisory Pty Ltd (**AZ NGA**).

AZ NGA is an Australian professional services advisory company established in 2014 that owns a number of financial planning and tax and accounting businesses with operations and customers across Australia.

AZ NGA is a subsidiary of AZ Aust Holdings Pty Ltd, whose major shareholders are funds managed by Oaktree Capital Management LP, a global investment management firm specialising in alternative investments, and Azimut Holding S.p.a., a global asset and wealth management business listed on the Milan Stock Exchange.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
• Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. the parties’ combined share in the supply of financial
planning services and accounting and tax services in
Melbourne, Victoria and across Australia is estimated to be
low and the increase in share of supply arising from the
Acquisition would be small
b. there are alternative suppliers of financial planning services
and accounting and tax services in Melbourne, Victoria, and
nationally.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
